payload.task_text:
I want to get organized for the Data-Driven Design course from Spring 2014 (its course code is DDD-2014B). Please look up this course and pull all of its assignments that have due dates.

Create an Excel file called "Assignment_Tracker.xlsx" in the workspace. The first sheet should be called "Assignments" with these columns: Assignment_Name, Due_Date (the date of the assignment's due_at field, formatted as YYYY-MM-DD), Points_Possible, and Assignment_Group (the name of the assignment group that the assignment belongs to). Sort the rows by Due_Date from earliest to latest.

Add a second sheet called "Summary" with two columns, Metric and Value. Include the following rows: Total_Assignments (the number of assignments with due dates), Avg_Points_Possible (the average points possible rounded to 1 decimal place), Earliest_Due_Date, and Latest_Due_Date (both formatted as YYYY-MM-DD).

Finally, create a calendar event for each assignment that has a due date. Title each event "Due: [Assignment Name]" where you use the actual assignment name. Set the event to start and end on the due date using the time from the due_at field. In the description, mention the points possible for that assignment.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently,

This is a small single-course task. The main agent completes it directly; do not dispatch any sub-agent. Canvas is read-only.

First resolve the task-visible workspace directory from the runtime allowed-directory listing (or the literal accessible-workspace directory already supplied by the harness), freeze it as `<workspace_root>`, and reject bare `/workspace` and dumps/run-specific paths. Call `canvas_list_courses(include_ended=true)` once and select the unique returned course whose code is exactly `DDD-2014B`; do not hardcode a course or assignment ID. If the code is absent or duplicated, stop.

For that returned course ID, call `canvas_list_assignments(course_id=<returned id>)` and `canvas_list_assignment_groups(course_id=<returned id>)` in native parallel. Use every distinct returned assignment with non-null `due_at`; if the list response is paginated, continue only until its returned pagination says complete. Join group IDs to returned group names, never to a guessed label. Sort by the UTC date component ascending, then assignment name. Compute literal `Total_Assignments`, one-decimal `Avg_Points_Possible`, `Earliest_Due_Date`, and `Latest_Due_Date`.

Freeze one literal canonical payload containing the sorted workbook rows, four Summary metrics, and one event payload per assignment. Each event title is `Due: <actual assignment name>`; start and end are the exact returned `due_at` instant; description is `Points possible: <literal points_possible>`. The workbook and calendar branch consume this same payload without recomputing dates or names.

Start the workbook operations and all exact-event searches in one native-parallel response. Create `<workspace_root>/Assignment_Tracker.xlsx` exactly once with only `Assignments` and `Summary`; use exact columns `Assignment_Name, Due_Date, Points_Possible, Assignment_Group`, UTC `YYYY-MM-DD` dates, literal numbers, and the four vertical Summary rows. Read both complete populated ranges back.

For each canonical event, search the relevant time/title before creation. Create only a missing exact event, at most once; never retry an ambiguous create. Read all retained event IDs back in one native-parallel batch. Accept only after the workbook and exactly one matching event per canonical assignment agree with the frozen payload, with no extra matching event.

nodes.text:
Task: Create an Excel workbook that tracks Canvas assignment data for the course "Data-Driven Design (Spring 2014)" (course code DDD-2014B). The Canvas data has already been pulled — use EXACTLY the data provided below. Do not query Canvas or any external system.

Deliverable: a file at exactly this absolute path (file name must be exactly "Assignment_Tracker.xlsx", placed directly in the workspace root, not in a subdirectory):
/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_GLM-5.3/SingleUserTurn-canvas-assignment-deadline-gcal/workspace/Assignment_Tracker.xlsx

Workbook structure — exactly two worksheets, in this order, and NO other sheets (remove/rename any default empty sheet such as "Sheet"):
1. First sheet named: Assignments
2. Second sheet named: Summary

SHEET "Assignments":
Header row with exactly these 4 columns, in this order:
Assignment_Name | Due_Date | Points_Possible | Assignment_Group

Then these 7 data rows (already sorted by Due_Date ascending — keep exactly this row order):
Assignment_Name | Due_Date | Points_Possible | Assignment_Group
TMA 25355 | 2014-02-26 | 10 | Assignments (TMA)
TMA 25356 | 2014-03-26 | 12.5 | Assignments (TMA)
TMA 25357 | 2014-04-16 | 17.5 | Assignments (TMA)
TMA 25358 | 2014-05-28 | 20 | Assignments (TMA)
TMA 25359 | 2014-07-09 | 20 | Assignments (TMA)
TMA 25360 | 2014-08-20 | 20 | Assignments (TMA)
Final Exam 25361 | 2014-09-30 | 100 | Final Exam

Data type requirements (important):
- Due_Date must be stored as a plain TEXT string in YYYY-MM-DD format (e.g., the literal string "2014-02-26") — NOT an Excel date/datetime cell, NOT a number, NOT a formula.
- Points_Possible must be stored as numeric values (10, 12.5, 17.5, 20, 20, 20, 100) — not text.
- Assignment_Name and Assignment_Group are text, exactly as written above (keep the exact spacing and capitalization).

SHEET "Summary":
Header row with exactly these 2 columns: Metric | Value
Then exactly these 4 data rows:
Total_Assignments | 7   (numeric)
Avg_Points_Possible | 28.6   (numeric; this is 200/7 rounded to 1 decimal place)
Earliest_Due_Date | 2014-02-26   (text)
Latest_Due_Date | 2014-09-30   (text)

Verification: after writing the file, read it back (both sheets) and confirm the sheet names and order, the header rows, the row order, and the cell values match the specification exactly. Ensure no extra sheets remain.

Report back: the absolute path of the file created, the sheet names in order, and a confirmation of the contents (headers + all rows per sheet), plus any errors encountered.
Build Assignment_Tracker.xlsx

Task: Create 7 Google Calendar events representing Canvas assignment due dates for the course "Data-Driven Design (Spring 2014)" (course code DDD-2014B). Use only the google_calendar create_event tool. Do NOT delete or modify any existing calendar events, and do NOT create anything beyond the 7 events listed below.

For EVERY event:
- summary (title): exactly "Due: <Assignment Name>" as given in the table below (include the assignment name verbatim).
- start.dateTime: the exact ISO timestamp from the table (UTC, with the "Z" suffix).
- end.dateTime: the SAME timestamp as start (the event starts and ends on the due date at the time from the due_at field).
- description: "Points possible: <points>" where <points> is the number from the table (e.g., "Points possible: 10"). The description must mention the points possible for that assignment.

The 7 events to create:
1. Title: "Due: TMA 25355" — start/end dateTime: "2014-02-26T00:00:00Z" — points: 10
2. Title: "Due: TMA 25356" — start/end dateTime: "2014-03-26T00:00:00Z" — points: 12.5
3. Title: "Due: TMA 25357" — start/end dateTime: "2014-04-16T00:00:00Z" — points: 17.5
4. Title: "Due: TMA 25358" — start/end dateTime: "2014-05-28T00:00:00Z" — points: 20
5. Title: "Due: TMA 25359" — start/end dateTime: "2014-07-09T00:00:00Z" — points: 20
6. Title: "Due: TMA 25360" — start/end dateTime: "2014-08-20T00:00:00Z" — points: 20
7. Title: "Due: Final Exam 25361" — start/end dateTime: "2014-09-30T00:00:00Z" — points: 100

Error handling: if a create call fails specifically because the API rejects a start equal to end (zero-duration event), retry that one event once with end set to exactly one hour after start (still on the same due date, same start time) and note the deviation in your report. For any other error, report the exact error message verbatim.

Report back: for each of the 7 events, the exact title, the stored start and end dateTime values, the description, and the event ID, plus an explicit confirmation of whether all 7 events were created successfully.
Create 7 due-date calendar events
